messages:
maria: heads up — we saw a sustained spike in exporter queue length for Tempo yesterday evening, tailing into Datadog and Splunk. queue_length went from ~200 to 12k for a subset of tenants. wondering if we should land a hedging/backpressure policy change or tune connector buffers first
kevin: ouch. do we know if it was a backend slowdown (tempo ingestion) vs. upstream burst? any per-tenant correlation?
anna: looked at traces — yes, mostly a reduced ingest rate from tempo in eu-west‑1. a couple tenants had very chatty span patterns + large parent traces (high fanout).
sam: gist: exporters are single-threaded per-connector slot and our outgoing TCP connections started piling up. we currently drop only when queue > max_queue_per_tenant, which is quite large.
jules: i'm worried about transparent drops. users can get silent loss. prefer graceful degradation: prefer routing lower-priority spans to cheaper/longer retention sinks (e.g., send to long-term bucket or sampling) and keep high-priority ones.
maria: agree on priority routing. but we need a short-term mitigation that doesn't require huge console UX changes. idea: per-connector slow_down_threshold that triggers latency-aware hedging to fallback exporter or temporary sampling.
kevin: proposal sketch: 1) expose connector metrics: queue_length, oldest_item_age, send_error_rate 2) add policy engine that maps metric thresholds -> action (increase sampling, route to backup sink, reduce batching size) 3) expose toggles in console for canary rollout
anna: +1. metrics we need: queue_len_per_tenant, drop_count, retry_backoff_seconds, current_batch_size. also emit an event when policy triggers so audit logs show why spans were dropped/rerouted.
sam: small config example i tried locally (otel-collector style):
```
exporters:
  tempo/primary:
    endpoint: tempo:3200
    timeout: 10s
  splunk/backup:
    endpoint: splunk:8088
processors:
  queue/primary:
    enabled: true
    max_items: 10000
    slow_down_threshold: 5000   # our heuristic
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [queue/primary]
      exporters: [tempo/primary, splunk/backup]
```
sam: rule engine would observe queue/primary.oldest_item_age > 60s -> mark spikes and flip sampling to 10% for non-critical tenants.
jules: how do we define critical vs non-critical tenants? we need a tenant tier field in the control plane and a default policy fallback. can the policy respect tokens/roles? otherwise ops will get flood of alerts.
kevin: we already have tier metadata in tenant config. extend it with telemetry_priority: [high, normal, low]. policy engine can use that + recent_error_rate to decide.
maria: UX note: console needs to show active policy overrides per tenant and a mini-chart of exporter backlog. ops should be able to ack and set manual overrides (e.g., pause splunk export for tenant X).
anna: ops question: if we route to backup sink (splunk/backup), do we maintain same attribute mapping? tempo/jaeger have different tags. we need conversion and a graceful mapping layer to avoid losing important attributes.
sam: yes converter layer required — we have small mapping util but need to make it pluggable per vendor. also consider rate-limited hedging: only copy up to N spans/sec to backup to avoid cost explosion.
observability-bot: alert: tempo-eu-west1-ingest-latency high (avg send latency 4.6s) — triggered policy check at 1719997200
maria: good — so next steps: 1) instrument and export connector metrics (queue_len, oldest_age, error_rate) in next PR 2) prototype simple rule-engine (metric -> action) behind a feature flag 3) add tenant priority metadata and default policy set 4) expose minimal console toggles and an audit log entry when policy fires. who wants to own 2 and 3?
kevin: i'll take rule-engine prototype (2). planning a small in-memory actor that subscribes to metrics and emits actions via control-plane API.
jules: i'll own tenant metadata + default policies (3). will add schema changes and migration script.
anna: i'll add the connector metrics (1) and update the exporter docs with mapping caveats.
sam: i'll wire the backup exporter hedging and add a rate-limiter.
maria: thanks! let's aim for a canary in staging by next Friday. please post small design PRs and tag #eng-platform-review. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: scheduled: canary deploy for exporter-rule-engine at 2024-06-07T02:00:00Z
kevin: quick question — should rule actions be reversible automatically when metrics recover? e.g., auto-unpause or should ops manually revert?
jules: auto-revert with cooldown sounds best. have cooldown and a manual override in console. we'll log both auto and manual changes.
maria: agreed. also add a debugging endpoint that shows current evaluated rules for a tenant so SRE can triage quickly.
kevin: ok will include that in prototype. i'll open WIP PRs today.
maria: cool. if anyone finds evidence of data loss earlier, ping me immediate and add evidence to the incident tracker.
kevin: noted. thanks all.
